title: Inventory: Foss et al. 2011 (PLoS Biol 9:e1001144) supporting information
intro: Generated by `ingest/inventory.py` from `sources/foss2011/raw/`: the ten supporting-information files listed on
journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article/file). PLOS serves them without file names; each is saved as
`journal.pbio.1001144.sNNN.<ext>` with the extension from its content (S1, S3 and S4 are Excel 97 workbooks).
The article page is kept as `sources/foss2011/article.html`; quoted facts used for provenance are in
`sources/foss2011/extracted/text_facts.tsv`. No code or data repository is cited: the paper says mapping and
quantitation code are available from the authors on request. Checksums are in `MANIFEST.tsv`.

roles.journal.pbio.1001144.s001.tif: Figure S1: protein-transcript correlations by transcript-level bin in the Lu et al. data (figure only).
roles.journal.pbio.1001144.s002.tif: Figure S2: between-gene versus between-individual protein-transcript correlation (illustration).
roles.journal.pbio.1001144.s003.tif: Figure S3: transcript-transcript versus protein-protein connections per gene (figure only).
roles.journal.pbio.1001144.s004.tif: Figure S4: isotopic strips (mass spectrometry, figure only).
roles.journal.pbio.1001144.s005.tif: Figure S5: MS2-identified peptide peaks (figure only).
roles.journal.pbio.1001144.s006.xls: Table S1: quantitation of 354 proteins (one peptide each) in 95 segregants.
roles.journal.pbio.1001144.s007.doc: Table S2: community membership (Word document; not parsed by the atlas).
roles.journal.pbio.1001144.s008.xls: Table S3: protein-transcript correlation coefficients for the 354 genes, with per-gene permutation cutoffs.
roles.journal.pbio.1001144.s009.xls: Table S4: genetic loci regulating protein and transcript levels: one row per linkage at 5% FDR (179 protein, 342 transcript), with the linked marker, chromosome and position.
roles.journal.pbio.1001144.s010.doc: Text S1: protein quantitation algorithm (Word document; not parsed by the atlas).

missing: No p-value, LOD, FDR or effect per linkage in Table S4, so the 1% FDR subset the text also reports cannot be separated and no direction (BY or RM allele) can be given.
No interval per linkage: each is a single genotyped marker (2,955 markers; 1,969 unique patterns).
No hotspot table: hotspots are described and plotted (Figure 3B, Figure 5) but not listed.
No list of which linkages are cis; the text reports counts at 1% FDR only (22 transcripts, 3 proteins).
No statement of the genome build; marker positions are consistent with R64 at marker resolution (see OPEN_QUESTIONS).
No mapping code (available from the authors on request).
